'''Jaylon Larone Tyson''' (born December 2, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]], the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech Red Raiders]], and the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]].

==Early life and high school career==
Tyson was born on December 2, 2002, and grew up in [[Plano, Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://calbears.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jaylon-tyson/22525|publisher=[[California Golden Bears]]|title=Jaylon Tyson}}</ref> He attended [[John Paul II High School (Plano, Texas)|John Paul II High School]] in Plano and helped the team win their first state championship in his [[Junior (education year)|junior]] year, during which he averaged 23.3 points, 5.8 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/texas/news/longhorns-freshman-jaylon-tyson-commits-texas-tech|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Longhorns Freshman Jaylon Tyson Commits To Texas Tech|date=January 9, 2022|author=Galatzan, Matt}}</ref> 

Tyson then helped them reach the state semifinals with a 26–2 record as a [[Senior (education)|senior]], being named the district [[most valuable player]] and a first-team all-state selection while averaging 22.3 points, 4.7 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 2.1 steals per game.<ref name="auto1"/> Ranked the 34th-best recruit in the 2021 class by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] after having flipped from [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/mens-basketball/2021/04/14/following-beard-tech-jaylon-tyson-joins-texas/7227192002/|newspaper=[[Austin American-Statesman]]|title=Once signed with Texas Tech, F Jaylon Tyson changes course, signs with Texas|date=April 14, 2021|author=Davis, Brian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/cal/basketball/jaylon-tyson-transfers-to-cal|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Cal Basketball Adds Texas Tech Transfer Jaylon Tyson|date=May 8, 2023|author=Curtis, Jake}}</ref>

==College career==
In his first year at Texas in the 2021–22 season, Tyson appeared in eight games, averaging 6.9 minutes and 1.8 points per game.<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/mens-basketball/2021/12/27/texas-jaylon-tyson-followed-chris-beard-ut-now-hes-transferring/9026264002/|newspaper=[[Austin American-Statesman]]|title=Freshman Jaylon Tyson followed Beard to Texas, now he’s transferring after eight games|date=December 27, 2021|author=Davis, Brian}}</ref> He then entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].<ref name="auto"/> Tyson ultimately committed to play for Texas Tech, whom he had previously committed to play for in high school before flipping to Texas.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/red-raiders/2022/01/09/tyson-scored-11-points-season-opener-against-houston-baptist-but-his-minutes-were-erratic-getting-do/9153979002/|newspaper=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|title=Former four-star prospect Jaylon Tyson decides to return to Texas Tech|author=Silva Jr., Carlos|date=January 9, 2022}}</ref>

Tyson started 31 games for Texas Tech in 2022–23, the third-most on the team, and averaged 10.7 points and 6.1 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/cal-s-jaylon-tyson-leaves-texas-tech-trauma-18481758.php|newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|title=‘On top of the world’: Cal’s Jaylon Tyson leaves Texas Tech trauma behind|author=Kroichick, Ron|date=November 12, 2023|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He ranked eighth in the [[Big 12 Conference]] for rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theathletic.com/4499732/2023/05/08/jaylon-tyson-transfer-cal/|website=[[The Athletic]]|url-access=registration|title=Former Texas Tech wing Jaylon Tyson transferring to Cal: What he brings to the Bears|date=May 8, 2023|author=Moore, CJ; Vecenie, Sam; Bass, Tobias}}</ref> He entered the transfer portal for a second time after the season, citing racist comments made by head coach [[Mark Adams (basketball, born May 1956)|Mark Adams]], who was later suspended and resigned.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/red-raiders/2023/04/16/tech-sports-roundup-jaylon-tyson-plots-transfer-according-to-report/70118850007/|newspaper=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|title=Tech's Tyson bound for transfer portal, according to report|date=April 16, 2023}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/2023/10/27/jaylon-tysons-texas-tech-case-ncaa-crackdown-on-second-time-transfers|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=October 27, 2023|author=Sweeney, Kevin|title=Jaylon Tyson's Case Is the Latest in NCAA's Crackdown on Second-Time Transfers}}</ref> He committed to the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/texas-tech-red-raiders/2023/05/08/former-texas-tech-forward-jaylon-tyson-to-transfer-to-cal-reports-say/|newspaper=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|title=Former Texas Tech, Texas forward Jaylon Tyson to transfer to Cal, reports say|date=May 8, 2023|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In October 2023, the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] initially denied Tyson's eligibility waiver for being a two-time transfer, despite his transfer reason being based on discrimination at Texas Tech, which the NCAA rules mentioned as valid criteria for an eligibility waiver.<ref name="auto2"/> He eventually was granted eligibility on November 9 and entered the team's starting lineup.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2023/11/09/cal-bears-basketball-gets-huge-boost-after-ncaa-approves-texas-tech-stars-eligibility-waiver/|newspaper=[[The Mercury News]]|title=Cal Bears basketball gets huge boost after NCAA approves Texas Tech star’s eligibility waiver |author=Faraudo, Jeff|url-access=subscription|date=November 9, 2023}}</ref>
